extracted.intended_audience: researchers and proposers responding to the DARPA Machine Common Sense (MCS) program; AI researchers and program managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing machine common sense capabilities as part of DARPA's MCS program, describing intended capabilities, core domains (intuitive physics, psychology, spatial navigation), and two high-level technical strategies (learning-from-experience and learning-from-web).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: "the basic ability to perceive, understand, and judge things that are shared by (‘common to’) nearly all people and can reasonably be expected of nearly all people without need for debate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that common sense is pervasive but often unstated background knowledge; includes understanding of the physical world, human motives/behaviors, and common facts held by an average adult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core domains of commonsense knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonsense background knowledge includes a general understanding of how the physical world works (i.e., intuitive physics), a basic understanding of human motives and behaviors (i.e., intuitive psychology), and a knowledge of the common facts that an average adult possesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These domains are singled out as primary targets for computational models of common sense and should be explicitly addressed by proposed approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability objective — understanding, reasonable behavior, natural communication, and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of common sense prevents intelligent systems from understanding their world, behaving reasonably in unforeseen situations, communicating naturally with people, and learning from new experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target systems that overcome these deficits — i.e., systems that demonstrate world understanding, robustness to unforeseen situations, natural human communication, and the ability to learn from new experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy 1 — Learn from experience (child-like learning of cognitive models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a service that learns from experience, like a child, to construct computational models that mimic the core domains of child cognition for objects (intuitive physics), agents (intentional actors), and places (spatial navigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches under this strategy should emphasize developmental, experiential learning mechanisms that produce models mirroring child cognition across the listed domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy 2 — Learn from reading the Web (librarian-like knowledge repository)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a service that learns from reading the Web, like a research librarian, to construct a commonsense knowledge repository capable of answering natural language and image-based questions about commonsense phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This strategy focuses on extracting and organizing commonsense knowledge from large-scale web sources and supporting QA over language and images as evaluation/use cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine common sense as computational services
rubrics_metrics.description: The program envisions machine common sense as a computational service, or as machine commonsense services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies an architectural expectation: common sense functionality exposed as services/components that can be integrated into other systems rather than only embedded monolithically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for generalization beyond narrow, specialized systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent advances in machine learning have created new AI capabilities, but machine reasoning across these applications remains narrow and highly specialized. Current machine learning systems must be carefully trained or programmed for every situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should prioritize generality and transferability of commonsense reasoning rather than narrowly trained, task-specific solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation modalities — natural language and image-based questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web-reading strategy aims to build a commonsense knowledge repository capable of answering natural language and image-based questions about commonsense phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating performance on natural language QA and image-based QA is an explicit intended use/evaluation modality for systems developed under the program.
